 Live Updates Updated Mon, Nov 2 2026 1:30 AM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Stock futures tick higher ahead of busy week of earnings, jobs data and the midterm elections: Live updates
 Justina Lee Sean Conlon Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, U.S., Oct. 30, 2026. Brendan McDermid | Reuters Stock futures moved higher early Monday after a losing week on Wall Street as investors braced for a packed week of earnings results, jobs reports and the upcoming midterm elections.
 S&P 500 futures traded up 0.5%, while Nasdaq-100 futures gained 0.9%. Futures linked to the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 186 points, or 0.4%.
 The moves come after the three major averages suffered a losing week, bogged down by selling pressure in tech as investors continued to scrutinize names related to the artificial intelligence buildout. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average each fell less than 1% on the week, while the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2%.
 In Asia, Japan's  Nikkei 225  gained 0.38% while the Topix declined 0.46%. The Kospi gained 2.38%, while the small-cap Kosdaq added 1.65%. Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was 0.53% lower. Hong Kong's  Hang Seng index  gained 0.61%, while mainland China's CSI 300 added 1.26%. 
 The week got off to a good start after Anthropic publicly filed for an IPO , which boosted AI-linked stocks. However, selling pressure resumed later in the week amid signs that capex spending could be abating after both Alphabet and Microsoft posted lower-than-expected capex forecasts . Amazon also left its full-year capex guidance unchanged .
 Still, 3Fourteen Research's Warren Pies isn't too concerned, pointing to a ramp-up in forward earnings estimates and adding that "there's a lot to like" about Anthropic's S-1 filing.
 "I just don't see anything broken with the AI trade fundamentally," he said on CNBC's "Closing Bell Overtime" on Friday. "Technicals are another story."
 The tech-heavy Nasdaq and the S&P 500 logged a losing October amid AI spending concerns, with the Nasdaq suffering its worst losses since March 2025. The Dow, however, rose almost 2% as investors rotated into defensive areas like healthcare.
 "Rather than running for the hills amid heightened AI risks, investors are seeing plenty of return potential in other types of stocks," Mike Dickson, Horizon's head of research and quantitative strategies, said in a note last week.
 Dickson added that while this week's midterm elections "have some investors worried that changes in Washington, D.C., could impact the markets, it's important to remember that stocks tend to stay steady regardless of which party gains control of Congress."
 The elections will be held on Tuesday, when Democrats are expected to take control of the House of Representatives, while Senate control remains uncertain.
 Investors are also awaiting October's nonfarm payrolls reading, which is scheduled for release on Friday and is expected to show an increase of 55,000 jobs on the month, according to economists polled by Dow Jones.
 In addition to the closely watched monthly jobs report, a fresh round of earnings releases is also due this week. "Magnificent Seven" member Apple is scheduled to report after the bell on Monday. McDonald's and Qualcomm are slated to report later in the week.
 22 Min Ago Oil slide accelerates amid reports of Mideast diplomatic talks 
 Oil prices retreated sharply early Monday amid reports that the U.S. and Iran are seeking diplomatic options to end the eight-month-long conflict in the Middle East.
 Brent crude futures , the international price benchmark, were down 3.02% at $110.01 per barrel at 1:20 a.m. E.T. 
 U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for December delivery dropped 3.31% to $100.65.   
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon Brent crude. —Hugh Leask 
 34 Min Ago Europe's stock markets set to start November higher
 FILE PHOTO: Bull and bear symbols for successful and bad trading are seen in front of the German stock exchange (Deutsche Boerse) in Frankfurt, Germany, February 12, 2019. Kai Pfaffenbach | Reuters Stock markets in Europe are expected to begin the first trading day of November in positive territory. 
 Stoxx 50 futures were seen moving 0.38% higher ahead of the market open.
 France's CAC 40 is set to start the session up 0.33%, with the Italian FTSE MIB advancing 0.21%, and Germany's DAX rising 0.18%. 
 The U.K's FTSE 100 , in contrast, is expected to trade 0.12% lower when markets open.
 —Hugh Leask 
 5 Hours Ago Mainland China and Hong Kong shares rise amid broad losses in other Asian markets 
 Mainland China and Hong Kong shares open higher after reports that Chinese financial regulators will meet banks and securities firms to discuss measures aimed at bolstering the country’s stock market.
 Hong Kong's  Hang Seng index  gained 0.59%, while mainland China's CSI 300 added 0.21%. 
 The gains in Hang Seng were led by consumer cyclicals and tech sectors, up 0.48% each. 
 — Justina Lee 
 6 Hours Ago Kioxia's shares fall 14% after company warned about stalling flash memory prices 
 Shares of Kioxia fell around 14%, after the company cautioned that prices for flash memory are stalling, during its earnings call last Friday.
 According to the Japanese semiconductor memory solutions firm, the average selling prices of NAND flash memory grew in the mid-20% range for the three months to September, compared with 70% in the prior quarter.
 Kioxia also expects to deliver a 2 trillion yen in operating profit for the current quarter, but that was lower than what analysts had expected at 2.35 trillion yen. This suggests that prices increases were nearly flat on-quarter.
 — Justina Lee 
 7 Hours Ago Japan's Nikkei falls 0.5%, South Korea's Kospi declines 1.4% 
 Asia-Pacific markets traded lower early Monday, tracking Wall Street's overall losses last week that was weighed by selling pressure in the tech sector. 
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  fell 0.54% while the Topix declined 0.74%.
 The Kospi dropped 1.39% at open, while the small-cap Kosdaq slipped 0.81%. 
 Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 was 0.24% lower.
 —Justina Lee 
 7 Hours Ago Oil prices fall
 Oil prices moved lower on Sunday night as U.S. equity futures rose.
 U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell more than 1% to $102.41 per barrel, while global benchmark Brent crude futures dropped more than 1% to $111.68 a barrel.
 The moves mark a reversal from Friday's gains of more than 2% , which added to crude oil's more than 10% rise in October.
 Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon WTI, 5-day — Sean Conlon 
 7 Hours Ago Asia-Pacific markets set to open lower as investors keep an eye on Mideast developments, U.S. midterm elections 
 Asia-Pacific markets were set to open lower Monday, tracking U.S. stocks which suffered a losing week that was weighed by selling pressure in tech.
 Japan's  Nikkei 225  was poised to decline, with the Chicago futures contract at 62,720 and its Osaka counterpart last trading at 62,420, compared with the index's previous close of 63,290.11.
 Hong Kong  Hang Seng index  futures were at 23,345, compared with the index's last close of 23,294.42.
 Australia's S&P/ASX 200 was 0.16% lower.
 Investors are keeping watch on developments related to the Middle East, as well as the upcoming U.S. midterm elections which will determine which party controls the Congress.
 — Justina Lee 
 8 Hours Ago Stock futures open higher
 U.S. equity futures opened slightly higher on Sunday evening.
 S&P 500 futures rose 0.2% just after 6 p.m. ET, along with Nasdaq-100 futures. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 103 points, or 0.2%.
 — Sean Conlon
